title: Transfer of alternating quantifiers
statement: Let $V$ and $V'$ be languages of bit strings, let $B,m\in\mathbb N$, and let $d$ map bit strings to bit strings. Suppose $d(v)$ has length $m$ whenever $v$ has length $B$, and every bit string of length $m$ equals $d(v)$ for some bit string $v$ of length $B$. Let $(F_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ be a family of maps on bit strings satisfying $F_{n+1}(\langle w,v\rangle)=\langle F_n(w),d(v)\rangle$ for all $n,w,v$, where $\langle w,v\rangle$ is the encoding that doubles each bit of $w$, appends $01$, and then appends $v$. For every $k\in\mathbb N$, $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, $n\in\mathbb N$, and bit string $w$, suppose every string $z$ obtained from $w$ by $k$ successive pair extensions satisfies $z\in V'\iff F_{n+k}(z)\in V$. Then the depth-$k$ alternating-quantifier condition on input $w$, starting with an existential quantifier if $b=\mathrm{true}$ and a universal quantifier if $b=\mathrm{false}$, with each quantifier ranging over strings of length $B$ and with membership in $V'$ as its depth-zero condition, is equivalent to the corresponding condition on input $F_n(w)$ with each quantifier ranging over strings of length $m$ and membership in $V$ at depth zero.
